cacheKey.normalizedQuery: story:B-3f3d Freeze REVIEW candidates and require bounded multi-lane finding saturation before remediation DEV B-cdf6 proved that four reviewer lanes were launched against one cutoff, but the first returned finding triggered a material commit before the remaining lanes terminated; later verdicts were bound to the old material and the Story re-entered REVIEW repeatedly. B-9812 reached 53 verified findings across 10 finding rounds, while B-74af re-entered DEV and REVIEW four times despite zero findings, so round count alone is neither completeness proof nor a safe optimization target. Implement one gate-consumed Frozen Review Inventory Epoch that binds a candidate to exact headHash, materialHash, storyFilesHash, scope and required lanes; runs independent discovery lenses plus the completeness critic; verifies raw findings and duplicate dispositions; and finalizes an inventory receipt only after all required lanes are terminal and one complete saturation wave adds zero new verified findings. An OPEN epoch must mechanically reject product, test, verifier and policy material mutation at the real write and commit boundaries. TIMEOUT, FAILED, CANCELLED, missing read or coverage evidence, duplicate reviewer identity, or a raw absence of output must never count as a clean wave. If the bounded wave budget is exhausted while new finding families continue, the lifecycle must require replan, decomposition, root-cause escalation or explicit human adjudication, never manufacture PASS. Finalization authorizes one remediation DEV entry with the aggregated finding inventory; it does not certify the old defective candidate, and any remediation material change requires fresh final review on the new material before TEST. Preserve all current required reviewer lanes, finding severity and evidence-state behavior, freshness rules, final validation, delivery and independent-host quorum. Explicit non-goals are atomic remediation closeout, PRE_CERT heavy-certification scheduling, evidence cache relaxation, lowering reviewer or host counts, and claiming absolute absence of all conceivable bugs. CHK-001 Represent the frozen review-inventory epoch and its receipt as signed gate-consumed process facts Create one deep owner for epochId, cutoff hashes, scope digest, required lanes, wave identities, host and prompt identities, terminal states, verified finding-set digest, coverage or read evidence, saturation result, state OPEN FINALIZED CANCELLED, and bounded-budget adjudication. Do not reuse audit-only signatureTag as gate authority without a new validated canonical duplicate or finding-family disposition contract. The receipt proves inventory saturation on the frozen candidate, not correctness of later remediation. CHK-002 Enforce the OPEN-epoch material mutation barrier at every authoritative write boundary While an epoch is OPEN, reject edits or commits that change source, tests, verifier, workflow policy, prompt contract or other review-subject material. Prompt guidance is insufficient: handler admission, Codex or Claude mutation hooks where supported, Git or commit checks, finding and pass binding, and lifecycle transitions must consume the same epoch fact. Explicit cancel invalidates unfinished verdicts for gate use and preserves them only as advisory history. CHK-003 Require complete discovery lenses and a verified zero-new-finding saturation wave before inventory finalization Run all scope and risk selected required lanes on the same cutoff, then run the completeness critic over the verified finding set. A wave is clean only when every required lane has a valid terminal receipt, mechanical coverage or bounded read evidence is complete, raw findings and duplicate claims are independently verified, and the wave adds zero new verified findings. Repeating the same reviewer, missing output, timeout, cancellation, unsupported host or prose-only PASS cannot satisfy saturation. New findings reopen another bounded wave on the same material; exhaustion requires replan, decomposition, root-cause escalation or human adjudication rather than PASS. CHK-004 Gate remediation DEV and subsequent final review on fresh inventory and material lineage A valid ReviewInventoryReceipt may authorize one REVIEW to remediation-DEV transition carrying the immutable aggregated finding set. It must not authorize TEST or certify the defective cutoff. The remediation commit creates new material and makes the inventory receipt historical; returning to REVIEW must compute impacted required lanes from the repair and dependency closure, require current evidence on the repaired material, and preserve full review escalation when scope or policy cannot be proven narrow. Replace the current Round 2 plus one-receipt shortcut wherever it could be used to claim sufficient final review. CHK-005 Prove the epoch reduces review churn without weakening escaped-defect assurance Replay the B-cdf6 RR-043 through RR-046 failure shape: after the first finding, material mutation must be rejected until all required lanes and the critic terminate and saturation finalizes. Cover timeout, cancelled lane, duplicate identity, forged duplicate disposition, scope expansion, related drift, stale receipt, wave-budget exhaustion and post-remediation regression. Record before and after DEV or REVIEW cycles and reviewer executions, but fail the optimization if escaped critical or high findings, historical mutation survival, post-cert source commits, stale acceptance or required lane and host counts regress. Round reduction is a metric, never a gate input. story intake repro-first stale-doc truth-first playbook runtime memory non-authoritative

devMemory.summary: A/B measurement of B-cee5 prompt stopgap: agents deviate from scan mandates either way, and no mechanical read-evidence exists to detect it.
devMemory.lesson: Old full-scan prompt: the agent silently disobeyed (read 1 of 111 decisions docs, no audit trail) yet asserted complete coverage — in production such deviation is invisible, so coverage claims under the old prompt were unverifiable; when agents DO obey, the 2.4MB corpus costs ~600k+ input tokens (the original exhaustion). New bounded contract produced equivalent review quality (same load-bearing gaps and same spec-contradiction OQ) at 74.8k vs 79.3k tokens with a recorded enumeration + candidate basis + explicit non-escalation reason. Core gap remaining: what a reviewer actually READ is self-reported prose, not evidence — there is no read manifest bound to scope_check_save/review_pass_set and no transcript-derived read log, so future before/after comparisons and compliance proofs (detecting unrecorded full scans) have no ground truth. Prompt-layer stopgap is instructional only; proof needs mechanical read evidence.
devMemory.reusePrompt: reviewer read evidence, scan compliance, token stopgap measurement, read manifest, scanEscalationReason audit, B-cee5 effect

devMemory.summary: A story whose diff includes package.json turns every later main merge into related drift: quorum, delivery-check, and review passes all stale and force a full re-review round.
devMemory.lesson: storyFilesHash covers the story diff file set. package.json is in that set whenever the story wires npm scripts (or gets scope-acknowledged version bumps), and DONE auto-bumps touch package.json on every merge to main — so any sibling story landing first changes YOUR story-owned material. Cost in B-3b05: one extra TEST->DEV->REVIEW round (4 reviewer lanes re-pass), fresh quorum_submit, fresh delivery_check_set. Mitigations: close stories promptly once quorum is bound; expect and budget the round-4 re-review when parallel stories share package.json; command-backed evidence must be actually re-run (refresh_stale refuses to rebind it silently).
devMemory.reusePrompt: stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch after merge / review assurance floor local rounds 0 after mergeMain / related drift package.json

devMemory.summary: Run quorum_submit during REVIEW, before advancing to TEST, once all active lanes have current-round passes.
devMemory.lesson: quorum_submit satisfies the 3x2 review-assurance floor by converting CURRENT-round signed review passes from ALL active reviewer lanes into host verdict records (hostA=claude-cli hostB=codex-cli); it refuses to fabricate. review_run_start/review_pass_set are REVIEW-phase-only, so advancing to TEST first (the round-2+ gate needs only >=1 receipt) strands the other lanes without a write path and forces a TEST->DEV->REVIEW round-trip to mint fresh passes in a new round. Correct order: all lanes pass in current round -> quorum_submit -> story_advance TEST.
devMemory.reusePrompt: review assurance floor blocked / quorum_submit missing current pass lanes / review_pass_set not available in TEST

devMemory.summary: Parallel reviewers' destructive dist bite-tests on a shared story worktree race each other; serialize them or use an isolated worktree copy.
devMemory.lesson: Destructive compiled-dist experiments (remove a registry name, run smoke, restore) must not overlap other reviewers using the same dist: a concurrently patched dist yields spurious FAIL observations. Either serialize the destructive step after all read-only lanes finish, or do what the round-2 quality lane did: build a scratch git worktree copy and bite there. Byte-restore and re-run the smoke afterward to prove the shared dist is intact.
devMemory.reusePrompt: dist bite test race, shared worktree destructive experiment, spurious smoke failure during review

devMemory.summary: ProofStory DONE shrinkage detector is a regex over summary text; shrinkage-flavored wording about neighboring items falsely blocks DONE.
devMemory.lesson: evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence (core/proofstory.ts ~1582) flags unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage via a regex matching out of scope, follow-up, not covered, deferred, excluded, partial, narrower etc. in the DONE summary. Describing a NEIGHBORING issue as out of this story scope / spun off as a follow-up in summary limitations trips the gate even when the story delivered everything promised. Fix by rephrasing (the sibling item is a different artifact owned by its own task; this story delivered fully) via summary_set, not by recording a false scope_shrinkage_decision_set.
devMemory.reusePrompt: unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage / DONE summary appears narrower than original snapshot
